title: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages: Equivalent Forms and Number Lines
seo_title: Year 7 Fractions, Decimals and Percentages Worksheets: Converting, Number Lines and Ordering (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: find equivalent representations of rational numbers and represent rational numbers on a number line
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on fractions, decimals and percentages for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7N04): converting between forms, simplest form, rational numbers on a number line, ordering and problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Fraction → decimal: divide. Decimal → percentage: × 100. Percentage → fraction: over 100, then simplify.
key_sub: On a number line, find what each small space is worth before you count.
body_html:
How it works

Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways to write the same amount. Percent means “out of 100”.

FractionDecimalPercentage
120.550%
140.2525%
340.7575%
150.220%
180.12512.5%
1100.110%

Fraction → decimal: divide the top by the bottom. Decimal → percentage: × 100. Percentage → fraction: write over 100 and simplify.

Example

Write 3/8 as a decimal and a percentage.

3 ÷ 8 = 0.375.

0.375 × 100 = 37.5%.

Answer: 0.375 and 37.5%

Example

Write 0.35 as a fraction in its simplest form.

0.35 = 35/100.

Divide top and bottom by 5.

Answer: 7/20

Example

Which is larger, 3/5 or 0.58?

3/5 = 0.6.

0.6 is larger than 0.58.

Answer: 3/5

Common mistakes

  • Writing the digits of a fraction as a decimal: 3/8 is 0.375, not 0.38 or 3.8.
  • Forgetting to multiply by 100: 0.4 is 40%, not 4% or 0.4%.
  • Mixing up tenths and hundredths: 0.07 is 7/100, not 7/10.
  • Not simplifying: 0.35 = 35/100 = 7/20.

faq.q: How do you turn a fraction into a percentage?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator to get a decimal, then multiply by 100. 3/8 = 0.375 = 37.5%.

faq.q: How do you write a percentage as a fraction?
How do I order fractions, decimals and percentages?
faq.a: Change them all into the same form, usually decimals, then compare.

faq.q: Can a percentage be more than 100%?
faq.a: Yes. 120% means 1.2 times the whole amount.
